rows.q: What is a SIP?
rows.text: A SIP invests a fixed amount in a mutual fund scheme at regular intervals, such as every month, usually through an automatic debit from your bank. Each instalment buys units of the scheme at its NAV, the market value of what the scheme holds, which changes every working day. Yours is ₹3,000 on the 28th of each month.

rows.q: how does sip work
rows.text: A SIP invests a fixed amount in a mutual fund scheme at regular intervals, such as every month, usually through an automatic debit from your bank. Each instalment buys units of the scheme at its NAV, the market value of what the scheme holds, which changes every working day. Yours is ₹3,000 on the 28th of each month.

rows.q: What is NAV?
rows.text: Each instalment buys units of the scheme at its NAV, the market value of what the scheme holds, which changes every working day. So the same amount can buy more units when the NAV is lower and fewer when it is higher. The fund's page in the app shows its latest NAV and your units.

rows.q: What's the minimum amount for a SIP?
rows.text: Each fund sets its own minimum; AMFI's investor site notes a SIP can start from as little as ₹500 a month. Yours is ₹3,000 a month now. A lower amount applies to future instalments. You can change it from Edit SIP, then Edit Amount & Date.

rows.q: Is my money safe in a mutual fund?
rows.text: Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. There's no assurance of returns, so the value of what's invested can go down as well as up. Early months can look flat or negative while the value moves with the market. I can't predict how it will move. SEBI's investor website explains how SIPs behave over time. I can explain this SIP's payments and options.

rows.q: How do I withdraw my money?
rows.text: To withdraw on Groww, open Mutual Funds, then your holdings, pick the fund and choose Redeem. The money usually reaches your bank in 3 to 4 working days. Some funds charge an exit load, a percentage of the NAV, if you withdraw within a set period. The scheme's documents state it. Tax-saving funds have a 3-year lock-in, and each SIP instalment is locked for 3 years from its own date. Stopping a SIP and withdrawing are separate: stopping ends future instalments, withdrawing sells units you hold.

rows.q: What is exit load?
rows.text: Some funds charge an exit load, a percentage of the NAV, if you withdraw within a set period. The scheme's documents state it. It applies to withdrawals, not to skipping, pausing or stopping instalments. The fund's page shows its exit load before you redeem.

rows.q: what does autopay mandate mean
rows.text: Instalments are taken by an automatic debit (autopay or mandate) from your bank on the 23rd of each month. Groww lists 15 possible causes in three groups: KYC and investor details, payment (autopay, mandate or balance), and scheme rules. The SIP's page in the app shows the autopay status.

rows.q: Is there a lock-in on SIPs?
rows.text: Tax-saving funds have a 3-year lock-in, and each SIP instalment is locked for 3 years from its own date. Other funds usually have no lock-in, though an exit load may apply. The fund's page states whether it has a lock-in.
